reasoning: Both remove the list from the shared module, keep the server-side checks, and fix the HUD errors correctly. A uses the exact RelocateToServerScriptService: true opt-out and a simple player-attribute signal that handles late arrival. B's RelocateToReplicatedStorage: false approach also works according to the library facts, but it doesn't match the rubric's specified mechanism and adds a new remote. A is slightly cleaner and better aligned.

criteria.note: AdminList.meta.json sets RelocateToServerScriptService: true as a boolean on the module itself.
AdminSharedService drops require("./AdminList") and IsAdmin; only AdminServerService requires it.
Server sets the IsAdmin player attribute; the client checks it at Start and listens on GetAttributeChangedSignal in case it arrives late.
AdminServerService:IsAdmin uses AdminList in onAnnounce; validation unchanged.
_HudClientSetup.meta.json ClientOnly true; HudClientService ClientOnly changed to boolean.
Changes are confined to AdminSystem and HudSystem; the luau-lsp failure is a checker path problem, not this code.

Uses RelocateToReplicatedStorage: false + ServerOnly on AdminList.meta.json; this keeps the module in place per the library facts, but it is not the RelocateToServerScriptService opt-out the rubric names.
AdminSharedService no longer requires AdminList, and a comment warns against adding it back.
The client calls the GetIsAdmin RemoteFunction in task.spawn with pcall, so the panel shows whenever the answer arrives.
onAnnounce still calls the server-side IsAdmin against AdminList; validation kept.
Same correct ClientOnly boolean meta files as A.
Adds a RemoteFunction model inside AdminNetwork (in scope); the luau-lsp failure is a checker path problem.

strengths: Attribute approach handles late replication and players already in the game
Remote answers only about the caller
weaknesses: Doesn't use the RelocateToServerScriptService opt-out the rubric expects
Adds a new RemoteFunction to the game
